title: Cases for the increment output
statement: For every Boolean word $s$, let $v$ be the fixed-width increment of $s$, with overflow represented by the empty word. Either $v$ is empty and the increment operation with default value $s$ returns $s$, or $v$ is nonempty, has the same length as $s$, and that defaulted operation returns $v$.
hypotheses_covered: $v$ is defined as the fixed-width increment of $s$, defaulting to the empty word on overflow
replaced:
For every boolean word $s$, exactly one of the following holds for the
fixed-width increment's output word: it is empty (overflow) and the stalled step
leaves $s$ unchanged; or it is nonempty, has length exactly $|s|$, and the
stalled step equals it.
